subject: Bun command compile wrapper vs raw command
decision: Merge Bun supplement OP-BUN-012 (raw provider-direct --compile) and OP-BUN-013 (effect-build staged atomic wrapper) into one canonical identity CO-BUN-12 whose provider_publication is provider-direct-durable and whose published_contract is atomic-published-durable (identity_owner = product-wrapper-over-provider-command). The raw CLI invocation is the implementation interior of the released compileExecutable, not a second public operation.
rejected_alternative: Keep two operations differing only in publication (Bun supplement's choice). Rejected because nothing in AGENTS.md or the decision record proposes exposing a raw non-staged compile alongside the staged one; two public operations differing only in wrapper staging policy would make the publication field encode product packaging rather than provider semantics.
governing_evidence: AGENTS.md compileExecutable retention; RECONCILIATION worked example (bun compile-executable atomic-published); Bun supplement OP-BUN-012/013 + E-EB-001
falsifier: A maintainer decision to expose both a raw passthrough compile and a staged compile as separate public exports would re-split this row.

subject: Deno compile publication law
decision: Correct the Deno supplement's output_publication for compile-executable and compile-watch from atomic-published-durable to provider-direct-durable at the provider-native level. No atomic claim for the final executable write exists in the supplement's own atomic claims (DENO-CL-047 describes appending and target-specific steps before publication; the only atomicity claim, DENO-CL-041, concerns the denort cache archive). The released wrapper's atomic publication is recorded in published_contract instead.
rejected_alternative: Adopt the supplement's atomic-published label for the native operation. Rejected as an evidence-to-guarantee conversion: documentation of a cache-side atomic write was silently generalized to the output executable, and compile-watch's repeated replacement has zero atomicity evidence.
governing_evidence: DENO-CL-041;DENO-CL-047;lifecycle lane Law D1/D2;RECONCILIATION-GATES lifecycle-specific publication
falsifier: An execution probe demonstrating that deno compile itself stages and atomically renames its final executable (and does so under watch) would restore the provider-native atomic label.

subject: Node SEA identity ownership
decision: Carry the three Node SEA operations as product-wrapper identities (published_contract atomic-published-durable for the two executable producers) with provider_publication recorded as provider-direct-durable, because Node's --build-sea and the legacy injector natively write their configured outputs directly; the staging/repair/validation/rename sequence is wrapper-owned.
rejected_alternative: Record six rows (three provider-native + three wrapper). Rejected: the wrapper sequence has no independent provider semantics; sub-operations carry it. Also rejected: recording only the wrapper identity without provider_publication, which would hide that the native command writes directly (the very fact that forces output redirection into staging).
governing_evidence: Node SEA supplement sections 5/12 and AC-MOD-001;lifecycle lane durable-file state machine;preflight-and-mutation-order
falsifier: None needed; the split field records both facts. If Node ever gains a native staged/atomic output mode the provider_publication changes with evidence.

subject: Rolldown lane
decision: Assign lane in-process-api to all Rolldown JavaScript-API operations, correcting the supplement's host-api. Rolldown is an installed npm library (JS package + native binding), not a host runtime API; host-api is reserved for Bun.build/Deno.bundle-style runtime-owned APIs. The lane definition's esbuild-specific wording (own native child) is generalized to installed-library API regardless of child-process vs in-process native binding.
rejected_alternative: Adopt host-api as the supplement wrote. Rejected: it erases the installed-library compatibility model (package/native coherence) that distinguishes esbuild/Rolldown from Bun/Deno and that D9/R3 must own.
governing_evidence: RECONCILIATION section 1 lane table;Rolldown supplement package-identity section;esbuild supplement section 4
falsifier: A future Rolldown embedded inside a host runtime as a built-in API would earn host-api rows at that identity.

subject: Deno declarations merged row
decision: Resolve D06 (API/command merged row) to the selected-command lane only: at v2.9.5 declaration emission is implemented in the CLI bundle path (emit_bundle_declarations); no host-api declaration mode is evidenced. Promote bundle --declaration to its own operation CO-DEN-06 because it adds graph/type-check work, a new failure class, and a distinct durable declaration topology; keep --check a sub-operation because it only gates emission.
rejected_alternative: (a) Keep declarations as a modifier of bundle-direct-write: rejected because failure and result laws change. (b) Invent a host-api declarations operation: rejected as unevidenced.
falsifier: If probes show declaration mode leaves the bundle failure law unchanged and merely adds outputs, demote to modifier; if a host-api declaration option appears in a tagged Deno version, add that identity.

subject: Rolldown handle methods vs esbuild handle methods
decision: Demote Rolldown close-reusable-build/close-watch-session/close-dev-engine from operations to release sub-operations (a release is the lifecycle boundary of its owner, not an operation). Promote generate and write to handle-bound operations CO-ROL-02/03 because their publication law is selected per call. esbuild's rebuild/watch/serve/cancel/dispose remain sub-operations because their publication law is fixed by the context's captured write mode. Grouping law GL-2: a handle method is promoted to an operation if and only if it carries a semantic-identity fact (publication or ownership law) not determined by its owning handle.
rejected_alternative: (a) Follow Rolldown supplement (methods and closes all operations): rejected — close has no request/result/failure law of its own and scoped-handle is not a lane. (b) Mirror esbuild exactly (split the Rolldown context by write mode): rejected — Rolldown does not capture output options at acquisition, so a context-direct-write acquisition identity would be fictional.
governing_evidence: RECONCILIATION section 1 (scoped handle is a lifecycle not a lane; Rolldown generate/write must be split by publication ownership);esbuild LAW-ESB-04;Rolldown E-ROL-HANDLE
falsifier: If a Rolldown version captures output options at acquisition, re-merge to context-memory/context-direct-write acquisitions; if esbuild ever lets rebuild choose write mode per call, split esbuild the same way.

subject: Bun compile memory-mode candidate
decision: Drop RECONCILIATION section 3's bun/compile-executable-memory and treat host-api compile as a single provider-direct-durable identity CO-BUN-11: tagged declarations give compile an implicit-or-explicit outfile and receipts observed durable executables; no memory result mode is evidenced.
rejected_alternative: Keep the crosswalk's candidate memory/direct-write compile splits. Rejected as speculative identities without source or receipt support.
falsifier: An output-topology probe showing Bun.build compile can return the executable purely in memory would create the memory identity.

subject: Rolldown vocabulary normalization
decision: Map the Rolldown supplement's invented vocabulary into the closed sets: scoped-acquisition/reusable/release/scoped-session/scoped-process-session/one-shot-with-cleanup collapse into scoped-context / scoped-process / one-shot with sub-operation releases; scoped-handle (as lane) is retired; no-public-value becomes caller-owned-value or none per actual result; owned-process-session becomes long-lived-handle; mixed-configured publication is an illegal state, so DevEngine is held as candidate-unresolved CU-ROL-01 until split by publication mode.
rejected_alternative: Extend the closed vocabularies with the supplement's terms. Rejected: each invented term either maps losslessly into the closed set or (mixed-configured) names an unresolved mode split that the key is designed to force explicit.
governing_evidence: RECONCILIATION section 1 closed lifecycle/ownership vocabulary;Rolldown PROVIDER-OPERATIONS.csv
falsifier: If probing shows an in-process session semantics genuinely distinct from scoped-context (e.g., provider-imposed lifetime not owned by any scope), extend the lifecycle vocabulary explicitly at that time.

subject: Reusable configured objects without release protocols
decision: Classify Bun.Transpiler construction and Rolldown ResolverFactory construction as one-shot operations returning caller-owned-value reusable configured objects, not long-lived-handle: long-lived-handle implies a release law (scope closure terminates/disposes) and neither object declares any release member. Constraint adopted: long-lived-handle requires a scoped-context or scoped-process lifecycle.
rejected_alternative: Bun supplement's {long-lived-handle, none} with one-shot lifecycle. Rejected as an illegal pairing: a handle with no release law is indistinguishable from a caller-owned value, and admitting it would let the ownership field promise a lifecycle that does not exist.
governing_evidence: Bun OP-BUN-001 ownership_contract (no dispose declared);lifecycle taxonomy (scoped handle requires Scope-owned release);gates ownership vocabulary
falsifier: A tagged version adding dispose/close to either object reclassifies it to scoped-context acquisition.

subject: Synchronous provider calls across providers
decision: Apply one cross-provider law: a blocking synchronous provider call may never be wrapped with an interruption promise. esbuild's five *Sync rejections are upheld (complete async twins, lost plugin authority, 16MiB ceiling, two absent hosts). Bun transpile-sync is deferred (async twin exists; only an honest non-interruptible wrapper would be truthful). Bun scan/scan-imports remain candidates because no async twin exists and rejection would erase the capability; they carry the same honest sync law.
rejected_alternative: (a) Blanket rejection of every sync operation: rejected because it erases Bun scan capabilities that have no async twin. (b) Blanket acceptance: rejected because esbuild's sync variants additionally lose plugins and hosts and have complete async replacements.
governing_evidence: esbuild ESB-OP-06..10 rationale;Bun OP-BUN-003/004/005 contracts;AGENTS.md interruption law
falsifier: If Bun adds async scan twins, transpile-sync/scan/scan-imports rejections align with esbuild's rule; if evidence shows Bun sync calls block unacceptably on realistic inputs, demote to reject.

subject: runtime-api lane discipline
decision: Reserve the runtime-api lane for capabilities invoked inside a produced artifact at artifact runtime (grouping law GL-3). Reclassify Bun.plugin/clearAll from the supplement's runtime-api to host-api operations (they execute in the build-host Bun runtime). Reclassify the crosswalk's node-sea/get-asset operation row into runtime capabilities RC-SEA-01..05, matching the Node SEA supplement; Deno compiled-runtime bundle observation is likewise a runtime capability (RC-DEN-01).
rejected_alternative: (a) Keep Bun.plugin in runtime-api: rejected — it erases the build-host vs artifact-runtime evaluation-phase distinction that D9 requires. (b) Keep get-asset as a build operation: rejected — it has no build-time invocation and belongs to the artifact runtime contract.
governing_evidence: RECONCILIATION lane table (runtime-api definition);Node SEA supplement section 2.1;Bun supplement OP-BUN-014/015
falsifier: A runtime-api item that becomes invocable during build composition (or vice versa) moves lanes with evidence.

subject: Bun HTML / full-stack / standalone-HTML
decision: Demote RECONCILIATION section 3's bun html-bundle-memory/html-bundle-direct-write (host + command) and full-stack-html-executable rows from operations to request modes of CO-BUN-06/07/09 (HTML entry as graph root) and CO-BUN-11/12 (full-stack compile), following the Bun supplement's atomic classification (C-BUN-066..077): an HTML or full-stack entry changes graph-root semantics and result composition but not authority, lifecycle, ownership, or publication law of the chosen build mode. Standalone HTML (compile+browser) is likewise a mode producing self-contained HTML, explicitly not a Bun runtime executable.
rejected_alternative: Keep the crosswalk's seven separate HTML/full-stack identities. Rejected under the section 1 rule: a mode is promoted only when it changes an identity-bearing law; none is evidenced to.
falsifier: A probe showing HTML mode changes the failure or publication law (e.g., different partial-output behavior for rewritten HTML trees) re-promotes the affected mode.

subject: esbuild context family
decision: Adopt the esbuild supplement's resolution of E03-E08: two context operations split by captured write mode (CO-ESB-11/12) with rebuild/watch/serve/cancel/dispose as sub-operations of the single state owner; no method has independent acquisition or release at 0.28.2.
rejected_alternative: Promote serve (socket/TLS owner) to an operation. Rejected: ServeResult has no stop member; release is only dispose of the whole context.
falsifier: An upstream version adding an independent release to any method promotes it.

subject: esbuild E01 three-way split
decision: Adopt the E01 split into build-memory, build-direct-write, and the rejected build-host-stdout mode (write:true with no destination prints bundle bytes to host stdout): three publication laws in one imported row.
rejected_alternative: Treat host-stdout as a degenerate direct-write. Rejected: the bytes are neither a returned value nor a file; the operation has {none;none} ownership and must be a typed preflight refusal.
falsifier: P-ESB-10 enumerates the exact option set reaching writeToStdout; over- or under-refusal falsifies the preflight boundary.

subject: esbuild E11 four-way split
decision: Adopt the E11 split into command-lane stdout one-shot, direct-write one-shot, watch (scoped-process), and serve (scoped-process): --watch/--serve are argv modifiers but change lifetime and publication, so section 1 promotes them.
rejected_alternative: Keep one CLI operation with modes. Rejected by the lifecycle/publication promotion rule.
falsifier: None; the split is forced by observed lifetime/publication differences.

subject: esbuild E12 reclassification
decision: Adopt the supplement's reclassification of E12: the shared native child is not a lane or effect-build process; its public controls stop() and initialize() are operations (both rejected); the child's ownership facts become architecture laws (process-global sharing, inherited stderr, first-use version check).
rejected_alternative: Treat E12 purely as a private implementation detail (imported inventory's stance). Rejected: two public exported functions control the shared engine and their misuse is a cross-owner hazard that must be named to be rejected.
falsifier: None; falsifiers live on the rejected operations (e.g. P-ESB-09 Bun unref behavior).

subject: compileExecutableMatrix
decision: Exclude compileExecutableMatrix from the provider-operation canon: it is provider-neutral product orchestration (deterministic cell identity, bounded concurrency, independent commits, complete outcomes, caller interruption law), not a provider operation. Its retention/removal remains pending-maintainer (question batch 1) and is out of scope for this crosswalk.
rejected_alternative: List it as a canonical operation. Rejected: no provider offers a native multi-target matrix; putting it in the provider canon would misattribute its laws.
falsifier: None; a maintainer retention decision would send it to the matrix-law program (R7) not to this canon.

subject: withJavaScriptBundle
decision: Map the removed Bun bundle continuation (D16) to CO-BUN-09 plus the borrowed-output laws: the capability survives as the native selected-command bundle identity; the continuation shape is retired.
rejected_alternative: none (decision D16 is final product intent)
falsifier: none

subject: Deno denort acquisition
decision: Keep D08 (compile runtime acquisition) as a declared sub-operation plus relations of CO-DEN-10, never a hidden fallback and not a standalone public operation: it has no caller-facing request/result surface independent of compile.
rejected_alternative: Promote acquisition to an operation. Rejected: its authority is entirely interior to compile; making it public would invite orchestration against a provider interior.
falsifier: If Deno exposes a public denort-prefetch command with its own contract, that new surface earns an operation row.

subject: Deno permission boundary
decision: Classify D10 (bundle permission boundary) as relations plus evidence coordinates on CO-DEN-01/02, not an operation: permission authority is part of each request/evidence coordinate. The 2.9.3 receipt contradiction stays an exact historical falsifier; v2.9.5 source resolves the declaration contradiction but not runtime certification.
rejected_alternative: Model a standalone permission-probe operation. Rejected: probing is R3 evaluator work not a provider operation.
falsifier: P-DENO-01 permission matrix outcomes become the evidence coordinates.

subject: Node SEA config modes
decision: Adopt request-mode/relation classification for S02/S03 (mainFormat), S04 build half (assets), S05 (code cache), S06 (snapshot), S07 (execArgv + extension policies): distinct config modes with their own version gates and admissibility relations, not standalone operations. Illegal combinations (ESM+snapshot; cross-target with snapshot or cache; CJS snapshot+cache ambiguity requiring canonicalization) are relations on the assembler operations.
rejected_alternative: Model snapshot or cache as operations (they execute code / generate artifacts during build). Rejected: they have no independent invocation; they are modes of the assemble/generate requests with version-gated relations.
falsifier: Exact-version probes (v25.7/25.8/25.9 ESM-cache boundary etc.) validate each gate; a mode observed to change publication or lifecycle law would be promoted.

subject: Signing boundary
decision: Split S09 (signing/verification) into: (a) target-specific candidate-correctness repair (stale-signature removal, macOS ad-hoc re-sign) as internal sub-operations of the executable-producing operations, with codesign/signtool as external platform primitives; (b) distribution-trust signing, notarization, containers, stapling, Gatekeeper excluded to the R9/M4 boundary with no operation rows in this canon.
rejected_alternative: One universal signing operation family in the provider canon. Rejected: D11 forbids flattening mutating/remote-job/verification kinds and the packaging home is undecided (M4).
falsifier: If M4 selects concrete Apple operations, they enter a future canon with their own lane/lifecycle (remote-job provisional).

subject: Builder/base relation scope
decision: Generalize S10: builder/base version equality applies wherever the participants are separate — legacy generator/base always, and direct explicit-base mode; direct default-base collapses the participants so no separate relation exists. This corrects the crosswalk's wording that confined equality to the legacy path.
rejected_alternative: Keep the crosswalk's legacy-only relation. Rejected: v26.7.0 documentation requires equality for direct explicit-base too.
governing_evidence: Node SEA AC-REL-001..003;section 6 of its report;S10 recorded falsifier (26.7.0 builder + 25.5.0 base failed)
falsifier: Exact-version probes per admitted line; a mismatched pair succeeding on an admitted cell falsifies the relation's non-overridability.

subject: Effect rows
decision: F01-F07 receive no operation rows: official Effect primitives are used directly (D2). Classified external-platform-primitive with an architecture-law claim each; wrapper-owned instrumentation only where the naming lane already allows.
rejected_alternative: Wrap Effect primitives in effect-build types. Rejected by D2 and FAL-001/002 heritage.
falsifier: none

subject: Cross-provider roles
decision: R01 (NodeMainProgram sealed main) and R02 (BrowserModulePayload as the narrowed successor) remain portable-role proof programs under D8 ship-if-pass; R03 (RuntimeExecutable) and R04 (CLI-text TypedWatchEvents) remain falsified; R05 (operation-owned surface boundary) is adopted — it is this document's key. No portable role is an operation row.
rejected_alternative: Include portable roles as operations. Rejected: roles are substitution contracts over operations; conflating them re-creates the flattened algebra.
governing_evidence: DECISION-RECORD D8;RECONCILIATION section 3 (R rows);browser-role decision table
falsifier: R5 proof outcomes; a failing role stays recorded with its falsifier rather than weakening the role.

subject: Bun scan pair
decision: Keep scan-source and scan-imports as two operations: upstream documents an explicit speed/accuracy tradeoff and different result surfaces (exports+imports vs imports-only), which is a result-law distinction the caller selects.
rejected_alternative: One scan operation with a fast flag. Rejected: the tradeoff is the identity; hiding it behind a flag would erase a documented provider distinction.
falsifier: Adversarial probe P-BUN family (scan-vs-scanImports accuracy) refines but does not merge the identities.

subject: Node SEA blob stage visibility
decision: Keep generate-preparation-blob as an operation row (distinct selected-command invocation with its own participants/relations/failure surface) but mark it an internal composition stage: it is not an independent public export candidate and its blob output is never a public durable result.
rejected_alternative: Demote to sub-operation of inject (crosswalk called it an internal stage). Rejected: it is a separately invoked provider command with its own identity/relations; hiding it would obscure the generator/base relation.
governing_evidence: Node SEA AC-OP-002;RECONCILIATION section 3 (S08 internal stage note)
falsifier: If the legacy route is ever modeled as one public pipeline operation, the blob row folds into it as a sub-operation.

subject: Watch identity form
decision: Adopt one identity form for all command-lane watches (Bun/Deno/esbuild/Rolldown CLI): selected-command / scoped-process / {long-lived-handle, provider-direct-durable}, raw byte streams, no typed events (falsified), scope-owned termination. Rolldown's in-process watch is scoped-context (no child process of the product's).
rejected_alternative: A cross-provider typed watch protocol. Rejected: falsified (R04) and reserved to D7's research routes.
governing_evidence: DECISION-RECORD D7;R04;provider watch rows in all five supplements
falsifier: D7 route experiments; upstream structured watch output adopted version-gated if it appears.

subject: esbuild serve disposition
decision: Adopt the supplement's defer for command-lane serve (bound address available only as human text; pinned-port-only honesty; Windows GHSA hole; zero executions) while context serve remains a sub-operation of the context operations.
rejected_alternative: Ship serve now or reject it permanently. Deferral is the truthful middle: the operation exists and is honest only under a pinned port.
falsifier: Upstream machine-readable address channel or an explicit product pinned-port decision unblocks; P-ESB-29/30 then apply.

subject: Historical raw NODE_JS_CODE route
decision: Treat the v19.7/v18.16 raw-JavaScript injection route as a separate rejected historical identity, never a weaker implementation of the modern preparation-blob operations; the modern route begins at v20.0.0.
rejected_alternative: Accept pre-v20 binaries as degraded legacy cells. Rejected: different resource contract and fuse; admitting them would collapse two route identities.
governing_evidence: Node SEA AC-RM-015;availability ledger v19.7/v20.0.0 boundary
